summary.title: Anomalous Hall effect from nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling
summary.authors: Longju Yu, Hong Jian Zhao, Yurong Yang, Laurent Bellaiche, and Yanming Ma
summary.executive_summary: This paper establishes a phenomenological theory for the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in magnets, specifically focusing on electric-field-driven AHE arising from nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling. While linear magnetoelectric coupling has been studied, the role of nonlinear terms remains largely unexplored. Using group-theoretical symmetry analysis, the authors demonstrate that a wide variety of magnetic point groups (MPGs) host AHE driven by uni-axial, bi-axial, or tri-axial electric fields. A key finding is that these electric-field-induced Hall conductivities are reversible by reversing the magnetic order parameter, a consequence of time-reversal symmetry and Onsager reciprocity. The study identifies 90 type-I and type-III MPGs that support such effects. To validate the theory, first-principles calculations are performed on two candidate materials: Cr2O3 and CoF2. For Cr2O3, the calculations show that σzy, σxz, and σyx conductivities are driven by Ex, Ey, and Ez respectively, with values exceeding 100 S/cm at 4 MV/cm. For CoF2, the conductivities respond via second-order coupling, with σyx reaching over 200 S/cm. The work highlights the potential of nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling for probing magnetic orders in spintronic applications, offering a new avenue for data readout in memory devices.

Electric-field driven anomalous Hall conductivities are reversible by reversing the magnetic order parameter.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper establishes a phenomenological theory for the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in magnets, specifically focusing on electric-field-driven AHE arising from nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling. While linear magnetoelectric coupling has been studied, the role of nonlinear terms remains largely unexplored. Using group-theoretical symmetry analysis, the authors demonstrate that a wide variety of magnetic point groups (MPGs) host AHE driven by uni-axial, bi-axial, or tri-axial electric fields. A key finding is that these electric-field-induced Hall conductivities are reversible by reversing the magnetic order parameter, a consequence of time-reversal symmetry and Onsager reciprocity. The study identifies 90 type-I and type-III MPGs that support such effects. To validate the theory, first-principles calculations are performed on two candidate materials: Cr2O3 and CoF2. For Cr2O3, the calculations show that σzy, σxz, and σyx conductivities are driven by Ex, Ey, and Ez respectively, with values exceeding 100 S/cm at 4 MV/cm. For CoF2, the conductivities respond via second-order coupling, with σyx reaching over 200 S/cm. The work highlights the potential of nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling for probing magnetic orders in spintronic applications, offering a new avenue for data readout in memory devices.

Research Context
The anomalous Hall effect is a fundamental transport phenomenon where an applied voltage induces a transverse Hall current response. AHE is an important platform for exploring topology-related transport properties and offers an efficient way to probe magnetic order. AHE was found to spontaneously occur in ferromagnets or antiferromagnets with specific magnetic configurations. Recent studies demonstrate that gate voltage can induce AHE via linear magnetoelectric coupling. However, the electric-field induced AHE arising from nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling remains largely unexplored.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central research question is whether electric-field induced AHE can arise from nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling in crystalline materials. The authors hypothesize that a large variety of magnetic point groups host an AHE driven by uni-axial, bi-axial, or tri-axial electric fields. It is predicted that such electric-field driven anomalous Hall conductivities are reversible by reversing the magnetic orders. The study aims to establish a phenomenological theory regarding spontaneous and electric-field driven AHE in magnets. Specific materials like Cr2O3 and CoF2 are hypothesized to host the aforementioned AHE.

Methodological Details
The study uses a group-theoretical approach to establish the phenomenological theory for AHE in crystalline materials. Symmetry analysis is performed on the entire 122 magnetic point groups (MPGs). Type-II MPGs are omitted because they exhibit time-reversal symmetry which forbids magnetization. The analysis focuses on 90 type-I and type-III MPGs for spontaneous or electric-field driven AHE. First-principles calculations are used to verify the theory in specific materials. Cr2O3 and CoF2 are selected as representative materials from the MAGNDATA database. These materials have no more than 10 ions per primitive cell, making computational costs affordable.

Procedures And Architectures
The anomalous Hall conductivity is expressed using the Berry curvature and Fermi-Dirac distribution. The Hall vector M is defined as (σzy, σxz, σyx) and behaves like the magnetization vector. The effective magnetic field Bα_eff is expanded with respect to electric field components. The expansion includes first-order, second-order, and third-order magnetoelectric coupling coefficients. For Cr2O3, the magnetic order parameter +L enables σzy driven by Ex, σxz by Ey, and σyx by Ez. For CoF2, the anomalous Hall conductivities respond to electric field via second order. The calculations involve varying the chemical potential with respect to the Fermi level.

Key Results
In Cr2O3, σzy, σxz, and σyx components remain zero in the absence of an external electric field. In Cr2O3, σzy, σxz, and σyx can be larger than 100 S/cm when driven by 4 MV/cm electric fields. The maximum value of σyx in Cr2O3, driven by Ey via third-order response, is less than 20 S/cm. In CoF2, σzy and σxz can reach 10 S/cm with bi-axial electric fields of 2√2 MV/cm. In CoF2, an electric field of 4 MV/cm can yield σyx being larger than 200 S/cm. Reversing the magnetic order parameter from +L to −L reverses the anomalous Hall conductivities in both materials.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The study emphasizes the important role of nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling in creating exotic transport phenomena. The reversibility of AHE by magnetic order reversal provides a robust method for probing magnetic orders. The symmetry analysis reveals that specific electric field configurations (uni-axial, bi-axial, tri-axial) are required to break symmetries and induce magnetization. The work offers alternative avenues for the probe of magnetic orders in spintronics.

Contradictions And Limitations
The study focuses on the intrinsic mechanism of AHE, excluding extrinsic mechanisms. Type-II MPGs do not host electric-field induced magnetization because electric field does not break time-reversal symmetry. For some MPGs, conductivity components might respond to electric fields via different mechanisms involving identical numbers of field components. The computational costs are limited to materials with no more than 10 ions per primitive cell.

Claims
Nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling can induce anomalous Hall effect in a wide variety of magnetic point groups. Symmetry analysis demonstrates that both type-I and type-III MPGs exhibit electric-field induced AHE from nonlinear coupling. First-principles calculations in Cr2O3 and CoF2 confirm the existence of electric-field driven AHE. Type-II MPGs do not host electric-field induced magnetization due to time-reversal symmetry. This provides a new method for probing magnetic orders in spintronic devices.
Electric-field driven anomalous Hall conductivities are reversible by reversing the magnetic order parameter. Onsager reciprocity relation requires that σαβ(+L) = −σαβ(−L). Calculations show that induced conductivities associated with +L and −L are opposite by sign.  This reversibility allows for efficient data readout in memory devices.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The study analyzes the entire 122 MPGs to ensure comprehensive coverage of symmetry cases. Specific cases like 4mm.1 MPG are discussed to highlight quenching behavior in fourth-order coupling.

Key Figures Tables
Table I lists the 90 type-I and type-III MPGs with respect to spontaneous or electric-field driven AHE components. Figure 1 shows the crystal and magnetic structures for Cr2O3 and CoF2. Figure 2 depicts the electric-field driven anomalous Hall conductivities in Cr2O3 and CoF2 as a function of chemical potential.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the establishment of a phenomenological theory for electric-field driven AHE via nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling in 90 magnetic point groups. 2. The strongest evidence is the first-principles confirmation in Cr2O3 and CoF2, showing conductivities up to 200 S/cm and reversibility with magnetic order. 3. The future path involves using this effect for probing magnetic orders in spintronic memory devices.
